newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Tight grip over Yugo inflation may cause tensions.
newsitem.headline: Tight grip over Yugo inflation may cause tensions.

text.p: Yugoslav central bank's tight control of money supply and inflation may lead to social tensions, a Belgrade-based economic think-tank said on Thursday.

"Keeping inflation in check will depend on how long the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) can maintain its tight monetary policy without provoking social tensions," Institute of Economic Sciences (IEN) said in its latest monthly report.
"There is no mystery about prices. The NBY has been sticking to a very tight money policy since the start of the year," IEN leading economist Stojan Stamenkovic told reporters.
According to the report, the central bank withdrew around 620 billion dinars in cash in the first two months of 1997.
M1 money supply in February fell to 5.157 billion dinars from 5.233 billion in January, and 5.495 in December, the institute said.
"Judging by the dinar movements on the black market, this is a substantial amount," Stamenkovic said.
The dinar black market rate inched up earlier this week to 3.7 from 3.8 dinars to the German mark on renewed lack of cash.
The central bank tightened its stance after a strong December monetary expansion pushed the dinar street value down to 4.3 to the mark early in January and threatened to re-ignite inflation.

Retail prices rose 1.0 percent in March against February, when they were just 0.6 percent higher on January. Cumulative retail price growth in the first quarter of 1997 stood at three percent. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
